answers.answer: Shuffle the Factory deck, select players + 1 cards face-down on the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Place one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: “randomly select number of players + 1” Factory cards; “one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories”; “one structure bonus tile”; “The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”

answers.answer: On the map, put the character on its home base and one worker on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining that base; four mechs start over their abilities on the Faction Mat, and six stars by the faction emblem. On the Player Mat, place six technology cubes on green boxes marked with a black square, four structures on matching boxes, four recruits on bottom-row circular spaces, and the remaining six workers on Produce's red rectangles; leave the one-time recruit bonus spaces empty and the action token beside the mat. The Faction Mat supplies starting power and combat cards. The Player Mat supplies starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 specify the starting map and mat pieces; step 3 says “set starting power and draw starting combat cards”; step 4 says “set starting popularity and take starting coins and objectives as indicated (two objective cards).”

answers.answer: You must move the action token to a different section from last turn, but may take neither action (a dead turn), either action, or both; if taking both, take top before bottom and never return to top afterward. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay a bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs before the action, then take as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefits as desired. Bottom-row resource costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades, so use the mat; never pay only part of a cost.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “different section from last turn”; “Bottom first is not allowed”; “First pay the full cost”; “You may use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost”; dead turns and Rusviet repetition are also specified.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Pay action resource costs using resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: “An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it and all its resources”; “Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities”; resources may be paid from “any territories you currently control, even to act elsewhere.”

answers.answer: No: on a normal unupgraded Move, the two selections are for two different units, each moving one adjacent territory; one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. All units can pick up, carry, and drop off any number of resources. Only mechs can also carry any number of your workers, never your character. A carried worker's transport does not count as its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself; likewise a worker may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's subsequent move.
answers.evidence: Move: “move up to two different units, one adjacent territory each; you cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice”; carried workers may subsequently move themselves.

answers.answer: A character or mech entering a territory containing only enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn. The enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero or insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. This is not combat. Your workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move: “Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops”; workers “immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources”; “Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero”; a worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order when there are multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: “Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order”; workers cannot independently move “into or out of” enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives a choice of two power or one combat card, before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. A built Monument also gives one popularity. Trade costs $1 and gives a choice of any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades. Put traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. If all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources. A built Armory also gives one power.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade sections state the $1 costs, choices, building bonuses, resource placement restriction, all-workers-at-home rule, and reshuffling/exhausted-combat-deck rule.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before producing; you must be able to afford all of it. Choose up to two different controlled territories, then each worker there may produce one token on its own territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce: “Pay every exposed Produce cost ... before producing”; new workers are taken “left to right”; “You may decline some or all production”; new costs affect “future Produce actions.”

answers.answer: Upgrade costs oil: move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box on the Player Mat, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: place any mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: “Upgrade — oil”; “Deploy — metal”; placement and ability effects are specified; completed bottom actions may still be paid for coins and ongoing recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Build costs wood. Put a chosen structure on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total may occupy a territory, including opponents' structures. The Factory is allowed, but lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A Mill supplies an extra Produce territory and produces as one worker, including when no actual worker is there, but only while you control its territory. A Mine is your personal tunnel for all your unit movement, including Factory Move, even when an enemy controls its territory.
answers.evidence: Build — wood lists the controlled-territory-with-worker condition, one-structure limit, allowed/forbidden spaces, and immovability; Mill and Mine descriptions specify their enemy-control behavior.

answers.answer: For Enlist, take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately take the selected one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, not by the one-time choice. For the rest of the game, when you or an immediate left or right neighbor takes the corresponding bottom-row action, you may gain its exposed circle bonus. Resolve the active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In a two-player game the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice. The circle bonuses are Upgrade: power; Deploy: coins; Build: popularity; Enlist: one combat card.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits sections give token placement, four immediate bonuses, the recruit-removal circle determining the ongoing bonus, neighbor scope/order, and two-player rule.

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly sets dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and their current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power. Rusviet People's Army permits one additional card total if any workers are present. If both sides have combat mech abilities, the attacker uses theirs first, then the defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial plus card values; attacker wins ties. Both players pay their chosen dial power from the power track and discard used cards face-up; card values do not deduct extra track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3 specify the dial range, card limits and Rusviet addition, ability order, simultaneous reveal, tie rule, dial payment, and face-up discards.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places an eligible combat star (normally no more than two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie protects only in its stated case: winning as aggressor on your turn. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4 specifies control, stars, retreat destinations, and resources; step 5 specifies popularity loss and the loser's card reward.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token, draw a card, and do this before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains of resources, workers, mechs, and structures go to the encounter territory where the character is. Pay the selected option's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs are paid and no additional mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses apply. Put the encounter card face-down on the bottom of its deck.
answers.evidence: Encounters: resolution is after all combats if the character remains; on a lost contested entry the token stays; “All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory”; no extra action costs or mat/recruit benefits apply.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary), must look at the available Factory cards, choose one, and return the rest. This applies to every player, not just the first visitor; each player gets at most one permanent card, and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section, with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Similar Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom Move action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement and stop restrictions apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: first finish of a Move action there requires each character to choose a card; later visits cannot exchange; Factory actions and bottom Move distances and restrictions are specified.

answers.answer: On your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, you may reveal a completed objective, but must meet all its requirements at the moment of reveal. Place its objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed. Saxony retains the other card after the first and may complete both starting objectives and score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: reveal only on your turn before or after a top/bottom action; meet all requirements at reveal; put both cards on deck bottom; Saxony may score both.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades; four deployed mechs; four built structures; four recruits; all eight workers on the board; one revealed completed objective; a combat victory (up to two stars, with Saxony's exception); 18 popularity; or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent even if power or popularity later falls, and another player's star never blocks a goal. The game ends immediately when a player places their sixth star.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists each achievement and says stars are permanent, other players' stars never block a goal, and the sixth star immediately ends play.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If a neighbor would earn a power/popularity recruit star, resolve it only after the active player finishes the action, in active/left/right order, and only if the game has not already ended with an earlier sixth star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to their prior territories; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: bottom-action benefits/coins/own recruit benefit precede the star; neighbor stars resolve after the active player and only if no earlier sixth star ended the game; pending unresolved battles are undone.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the rates are $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources. Thus five stars score $20; four ordinary territories plus the Factory count as seven territories and score $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs and score $12. These categories add $53 to held coins, before any structure bonus. You earn the selected structure bonus even if enemies control your structures' territories; only the selected tile scores. Victory goes to the most total coins. Ties break in order by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and example give the 10-popularity rates and $53 calculation; structure bonus says it is earned even if enemies control those territories; final tie-break list specifies the order.
